cases.description: Microsoft's documented example: periods required for 2,000 to reach 2,200 at 2.5% per period
cases.expected_note: Excel documents this example's result as 3.86 periods. Derived from the documented formula (LN(fv) - LN(pv)) / LN(1 + rate) = LN(1.1)/LN(1.025) = 3.85986616

cases.description: Documented example: months for 1,000 to reach 1,200 at 2.5% annual interest
cases.expected_note: Excel documents this example's result as 87.6 months. Same formula with a monthly rate of 0.025/12 -> LN(1.2)/LN(1+0.0020833) = 87.60547642

cases.description: A clean closed-form case: doubling at a 100% rate takes exactly one period
A rate of zero makes LN(1+rate) zero, so the value never grows
cases.expected_note: Excel documents #NUM! if rate is less than or equal to 0 (with no growth the target is never reached)

cases.description: A non-positive future value is outside the logarithm's domain
cases.expected_note: Excel documents #NUM! if pv or fv is less than or equal to 0, since the formula takes their natural logarithms
